## PR Description

Fixes #2227

## Root cause

The `loading test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart` red is the **loopback-ws loader-drop family** (issue #2331): under CI-leg load, dart test's loader WebSocket (`127.0.0.1:<port>/…/ws`) to a freshly spawned test VM dies mid-handshake — `Failed to load "…": Connection closed before full header was received`. The victim file is arbitrary (whatever is loading when the socket dies); every test that ran stays green. All 4 jsr_cli_test.dart reds (runs 43861013338, 43994366865, 44149246706, 44167780049 — 4 distinct SHAs, incl. both drilled job logs at FILE-level identity: `89 tests passed, 1 failed`, failure surfaced ~6 s into the load phase) were loader drops, never assertions. #2331 landed the class fix (one-shot rerun wrapper `scripts/load_drop_retry.sh`) on the sharded legs — but the jsr trio was the last unhealed surface.

## Delivered

- **ci.yml test-core trio wrapped** (shard 0 step): `bash scripts/load_drop_retry.sh` around `dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage` + the 3 jsr files, with its own `--file-reporter=json:build/test-results/cli-trio-lcov.json` (wrapper's failed-inventory feed; rerun inherits coverage, so healed hits land in the same lcov merge).
- **scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core wrapped** identically — the two unshielded legs from the issue triage note now heal drops at runtime.
- **Un-quarantined** `test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart` (entry removed from scripts/test_quarantine.json): with every leg that runs the file load-drop-safe, the #2228 skip was pure loss — it dropped the file from the PTY shard selection (the CLI coverage ratchet's jsr hits, gh-1033) while integration-mock never selected it anyway (finds test/integration only). Follows the un-quarantine-in-fix-PR precedent (#2161).
- **Guards**: new `test/ci_jsr_trio_load_drop_guard_test.dart` pins both wirings (wrapper + logs + flags + 3-file list in sync), asserts no junit consumer reads the trio logs, and pins the un-quarantine. `test/ci_load_drop_retry_guard_test.dart` AC1/AC3 updated mechanically (test-core now has 2 wrapped steps; shard step picked by its own log name) — docstring-only edits in that file belong to the parallel #2331 lane, hunks disjoint.

## Verification

- Dart 3.14.1 (exact CI pin) standalone SDK in-worktree: guard + wrapper tests 17/17; the real trio run **through the wrapper** 45/45 green (exit 0, reporter log written, no retry log on a green attempt).
- `dart format` clean, `dart analyze`: 0 issues in touched files (the 78 package issues are pre-existing on main, untouched paths — office_addin etc.).
- `apply_quarantine.py --check` OK (13 entries), `bash -n` on ci_fast_gate.sh OK.

## Remaining / notes

- The load-drop class itself is dart-test loader infra; the repo-level root fix is the retry-wrapper family (#2331). The #2331 lane's in-flight bounded-retry upgrade drops in transparently under these invocations (argv unchanged).
- flake_watch.py keeps scanning junit-integration-shard-* artifacts only; with the trio wrapped, its drops now heal at runtime and no longer surface as reds to watch.

A rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only with a written justification** in the census (the thread reply and the response summary: why this is not maintainability debt). ## Description

Fixes #2227

## Root cause

The `loading test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart` red is the **loopback-ws loader-drop family** (issue #2331): under CI-leg load, dart test's loader WebSocket (`127.0.0.1:<port>/…/ws`) to a freshly spawned test VM dies mid-handshake — `Failed to load "…": Connection closed before full header was received`. The victim file is arbitrary (whatever is loading when the socket dies); every test that ran stays green. All 4 jsr_cli_test.dart reds (runs 43861013338, 43994366865, 44149246706, 44167780049 — 4 distinct SHAs, incl. both drilled job logs at FILE-level identity: `89 tests passed, 1 failed`, failure surfaced ~6 s into the load phase) were loader drops, never assertions. #2331 landed the class fix (one-shot rerun wrapper `scripts/load_drop_retry.sh`) on the sharded legs — but the jsr trio was the last unhealed surface.

## Delivered

- **ci.yml test-core trio wrapped** (shard 0 step): `bash scripts/load_drop_retry.sh` around `dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage` + the 3 jsr files, with its own `--file-reporter=json:build/test-results/cli-trio-lcov.json` (wrapper's failed-inventory feed; rerun inherits coverage, so healed hits land in the same lcov merge).
- **scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core wrapped** identically — the two unshielded legs from the issue triage note now heal drops at runtime.
- **Un-quarantined** `test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart` (entry removed from scripts/test_quarantine.json): with every leg that runs the file load-drop-safe, the #2228 skip was pure loss — it dropped the file from the PTY shard selection (the CLI coverage ratchet's jsr hits, gh-1033) while integration-mock never selected it anyway (finds test/integration only). Follows the un-quarantine-in-fix-PR precedent (#2161).
- **Guards**: new `test/ci_jsr_trio_load_drop_guard_test.dart` pins both wirings (wrapper + logs + flags + 3-file list in sync), asserts no junit consumer reads the trio logs, and pins the un-quarantine. `test/ci_load_drop_retry_guard_test.dart` AC1/AC3 updated mechanically (test-core now has 2 wrapped steps; shard step picked by its own log name) — docstring-only edits in that file belong to the parallel #2331 lane, hunks disjoint.

## Verification

- Dart 3.14.1 (exact CI pin) standalone SDK in-worktree: guard + wrapper tests 17/17; the real trio run **through the wrapper** 45/45 green (exit 0, reporter log written, no retry log on a green attempt).
- `dart format` clean, `dart analyze`: 0 issues in touched files (the 78 package issues are pre-existing on main, untouched paths — office_addin etc.).
- `apply_quarantine.py --check` OK (13 entries), `bash -n` on ci_fast_gate.sh OK.

## Remaining / notes

- The load-drop class itself is dart-test loader infra; the repo-level root fix is the retry-wrapper family (#2331). The #2331 lane's in-flight bounded-retry upgrade drops in transparently under these invocations (argv unchanged).
- flake_watch.py keeps scanning junit-integration-shard-* artifacts only; with the trio wrapped, its drops now heal at runtime and no longer surface as reds to watch.

- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.

- `lib/src/agent/` — FinalizeGate, tool pairing, session image registry.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — trajectory ledger core; goldens under `test/trajectory/goldens/`.

- `lib/src/model_roles/` — roles/fallbacks/keyring/watchdogs + provider catalog; `lib/src/ttsr/` — streaming-interrupt rules.
- `lib/src/skills/`, `lib/src/prompts/` — skills discovery; AGENTS/CLAUDE/GOAL/DESIGN auto-merge into the system prompt.
- `lib/src/task/`, `lib/src/messaging/`, `lib/src/session/attach/` — subagents, inbox fabric, attached sessions → `docs/subagents/README.md`.

- `bin/fah.dart` + `lib/src/cli/` — the `fa` CLI: REPL, slash commands, headless/serve modes → `docs/agents/cli.md`.

## Hard architecture rules (stay inline)

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart`: grouped **APPEND-ONLY** export
  sections — one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted by path
  within a group, new exports append to their group. No mini-barrels, no
  re-sorting (gh-1232).
- God-file ceiling: no `.dart` file over **2800** lines (crap4dart `loc`
  gate). Target < 2000 for primary files; split by concern into `part`
  files — never by extracting public API.

## Working in parallel (shared checkout + worktrees)

Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked; run no
heavy commands (full suites/analyze) in it; never `git stash` the user's
WIP; talk to peer agents through the messaging fabric, not their files.
Worktrees only if genuinely required — ask first, create detached under
`.worktrees/<name>/` from the remote tracking ref, remove when done.
Full policy: `docs/agents/parallel-worktrees.md`.

## Memory (footnote)

Before any non-trivial task, **search memory first** (`memory_search`,
then `memory_list` for fuzzy topics). Scopes: **project** = this repo
(`.fah/memory/note/` since gh-2185 — local-only, not committed; the
user's files: read freely, write only via `memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts
only; supersede by delete + add — never leave solved problems to rot. The
host recomposes the `<memory>` prompt section after every add; tool wiring
is `memoryTools` + `lib/src/memory/`. Churn pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`;
usage details: `docs/agents/memory-usage.md`.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done: coverage first (`test/goldens/` + `golden_guard_test.dart`
map), real fonts (`ensureGoldenFonts`), full frames (1280x800 / 390x844),
determinism, eyes on pixels after `--update-goldens`, green
`flutter test test/goldens` + `scripts/check_goldens.py` (orphan snapshots
hard-fail). Full rules: `docs/agents/golden-tests.md`.

## Prompts live outside Dart code

Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (YAML frontmatter,
`{{token}}` placeholders) — never string literals in `.dart`. After
editing: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` regenerates the `.g.dart`
files (`test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` gates drift); Codex catalog
refresh: `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Details:
`docs/agents/prompts.md`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The hook is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI classifies
PRs through the same script (`--dry-run`) — one classifier, one threshold
set, hook/CI parity via `GATE_STAGE` markers. Path rules: docs/markdown/
prompts-only → size + analyze; lib/bin/test/pubspec → +tests, coverage,
CRAP, dup, dupx; `test/integration/**` → +integration-mock;
flutter_app/packages → +flutter; scripts/.github → everything. Invariants:

  the tag-only provider smoke + nightly).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80%; jscpd < 1% core / < 3.7% app; cross-module

- Red-in-≥2-distinct-SHA-runs flakes quarantine via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json`; nightly keeps running quarantined files.

Full gate text: `docs/agents/quality-gates.md`; CI workflows: `docs/ci.md`.

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type exists on BOTH the CLI
and the Flutter app unless fundamentally impossible — then it MUST be in
`cliOnlySettings`/`appOnlySettings` (`lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# load_drop_retry.sh — one-shot loopback-ws load-drop retry for sharded
# dart test legs (issue #2331).
#
# Family: under CI-leg load the dart test loader's loopback WebSocket
# (127.0.0.1:…/ws) to a freshly spawned test VM can die mid-handshake —
#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection closed before full header was
#   received, uri = http://127.0.0.1:…/ws
#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection reset by peer, uri=http://127.0.0.1:…/ws
# The victim file is arbitrary (whatever is loading when the socket dies),
# never an assertion failure (6/6 occurrences on the card). The shard reds
# even though every test that ran was green.
#
# This wrapper runs the shard's dart test command as given, and on failure
# that carries BOTH the `Failed to load "<path>"` marker AND a ws-drop
# signature, re-runs the failed inventory ONCE (the gh-1026
# rerun-only-failed-files discipline): the ws-dropped files PLUS every
# attempt-1 failed suite the main reporter log records (via the repo's
# scripts/gate_failed_targets.py). A co-occurring real failure — assertion
# failure or compile-error load failure — is therefore IN the rerun and
# keeps the shard red; an attempt 1 whose only failures are ws drops heals.
# Without the ws-drop signature the wrapper never reruns at all: real
# failures stay loud, nothing is rerun blind, nothing is masked.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/load_drop_retry.sh <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> "<targets>"
#
#   <main-log>   the path of the caller's own --file-reporter=json:<main-log>
#                (passed as part of <cmd...>) that junit/duration consumers
#                read — attempt-1 evidence is never clobbered; also names
#                the <main-log>.console capture;
#   <retry-log>  where the rerun's reporter writes (kept separate so the
#                main log is never overwritten);
#   <cmd...>     the full dart test invocation INCLUDING its own
#                --file-reporter flag; the FINAL argument is the quoted,
#                space-separated target list (word-split here).
#
# Exit: 0 when the run (or the single rerun) is green; the failing exit
# code otherwise. Coverage consumers are safe: the rerun inherits
# --coverage=coverage, so a healed file's hits land in the same coverage/
# dir the gate merges.
set -euo pipefail
# TARGETS/RERUN_TARGETS expand unquoted below (word-split by design — the
# caller passes a quoted, space-separated list). Glob-off: a path carrying
# glob metacharacters must never expand (PR #2347 review digest).
set -f

usage() {
  echo "usage: $0 <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> \"<targets>\"" >&2
  exit 2
}

[ "$#" -ge 5 ] || usage
MAIN_LOG=$1
RETRY_LOG=$2
[ "${3:-}" = "--" ] || usage
shift 3
CMD=("${@:1:$#-1}")       # command + flags (including --file-reporter=…)
TARGETS="${!#}"           # final arg: quoted, space-separated target list
[ -n "$TARGETS" ] || usage

CONSOLE="${MAIN_LOG}.console"

# Attempt 1 — the command exactly as the step defines it (its own
# --file-reporter=json:<main-log> is part of CMD; dart accumulates repeated
# reporter flags, so the wrapper must not add a second one).
set +e
"${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS 2>&1 | tee "$CONSOLE"
RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
set -e
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Detection: the ws-drop family signature ONLY — it gates WHETHER this
# wrapper reruns at all. A real assertion failure, compile error, or
# timeout never pairs `Failed to load "…"` with ws text (that prefix is
# emitted solely by the test loader) — with no signature the failure is
# deterministic runner territory: exit here, loud, no rerun.
if ! grep -qE 'Connection closed before full header was received|Connection reset by peer' \
    "$CONSOLE"; then
  echo "load_drop_retry: failure carries no loopback-ws drop signature — not rerunning" >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi
DROPPED=$(awk '/Failed to load/ && (/Connection closed before full header was received/ || /Connection reset by peer/)' \
  "$CONSOLE" |
  sed -E -e 's/.*Failed to load "([^"]+)".*/\1/' -e 't' -e 's/.*Failed to load ([^:"]+):.*/\1/' |
  sort -u)
# WHAT to rerun is the FULL attempt-1 failed inventory, not just the
# ws-dropped files (PR #2347 review round 1, blocking): union the console
# drops with every failed suite the attempt-1 reporter recorded
# (gate_failed_targets.py — failure AND error results, load failures via
# the hidden `loading <path>` tests; missing/unparsable log = clean empty).
# A co-occurring real failure is therefore IN the rerun and fails it — the
# shard stays red; an attempt 1 whose ONLY failures are ws drops heals.
REPORTER_FAILED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$MAIN_LOG")
RERUN_TARGETS=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$DROPPED" "$REPORTER_FAILED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)
if [ -z "$RERUN_TARGETS" ]; then
  echo "load_drop_retry: ws-drop signature present but no failed-file inventory — not rerunning blind" >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

echo "🔁 load-drop retry (#2331): rerunning failed file(s) ONCE:" >&2
printf '%s\n' "$RERUN_TARGETS" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2

RETRY_CMD=()
for arg in "${CMD[@]}"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --file-reporter=*) ;;            # rerun writes to RETRY_LOG instead
    *) RETRY_CMD+=("$arg") ;;
  esac
done

set +e
"${RETRY_CMD[@]}" --file-reporter="json:$RETRY_LOG" $RERUN_TARGETS 2>&1 | tee -a "$CONSOLE"
RETRY_RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
set -e

if [ "$RETRY_RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "✅ load-drop retry: healed — dropped file(s) green on the rerun" >&2
  exit 0
fi
echo "❌ load-drop retry: rerun still red (exit $RETRY_RC) — failing loudly" >&2
exit "$RETRY_RC"

timeout-minutes: 2
        continue-on-error: true

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
        timeout-minutes: 2
        continue-on-error: true

      # gh-2072 (review thread 5): the prewarm is scope-gated EXACTLY like
      # the pub get above it — on an out-of-scope PR checkout/setup-dart/
      # pub get are all skipped (the fastpass keeps the leg green in
      # seconds) and an unconditional prewarm would red the required
      # contexts: the composite action file isn't even on disk without
      # checkout, and the script hard-fails without the pub get's package
      # config.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p build/test-results
          # Issue #2331: under CI-leg load the dart test loader's loopback ws
          # to a spawning test VM dies mid-handshake ("Failed to load …:
          # Connection closed before full header was received / Connection
          # reset by peer") — an arbitrary victim file, 6/6 occurrences on
          # this leg family. The wrapper re-runs ONLY that dropped file once
          # (gh-1026 rerun-only-failed discipline); real failures carry no
          # ws-drop signature and stay loud. junit below still reads the
          # attempt-1 main log — a healed rerun writes to …retry.json.
          bash scripts/load_drop_retry.sh \
            "build/test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            "build/test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.retry.json" \
            -- \
            dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:build/test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            "$targets"
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            build/test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            build/test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/test-results
          # Issue #2227: the trio rides NO quarantine filter (gh-1033: the
          # CLI coverage ratchet needs these hits on every core/shared PR),
          # so the #2331 loopback-ws load-drop family reached this leg
          # unhealed — a dropped loader ws reds the gate on an arbitrary
          # victim file while every test that ran was green (4/4 jsr_cli
          # reds were loader drops, never assertions). Same one-shot
          # wrapper as the sharded legs: a dropped file reruns ONCE (the
          # rerun inherits --coverage=coverage, so healed hits land in
          # this shard's coverage dir); real failures carry no ws-drop
          # signature and stay loud. No junit consumer reads these logs —
          # the trio feeds the lcov merge only.
          bash scripts/load_drop_retry.sh \
            "build/test-results/cli-trio-lcov.json" \
            "build/test-results/cli-trio-lcov.retry.json" \
            -- \
            dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:build/test-results/cli-trio-lcov.json" \
            "test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart"

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      # gh-1724: the shard evidence uploads ride the gh-1412 one-shot retry —
      # run 39432336443 (tag v1.0.611) red'd shard 3 with every test GREEN on
      # a single transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: 404 artifact not
      # found` from GitHub's blob storage; the Quality gate followed
      # (`a leg is failure (test-core)`) and the release went red. Same
      # shape as the pty leg: the retry re-runs the SAME pinned action with
      # overwrite:true (a failed attempt leaves the artifact half-registered
      # — without overwrite the retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely
      # dead endpoint still fails the shard loudly.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_core_coverage
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry coverage upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: >-
          always() && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
          && steps.upload_core_coverage.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info

# gh-1538: the publish dry-run below rehearses the tag-stamped
          # stage (gh-1522), moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — tag math needs the full tag graph
          # (blobless per gh-1477, same incantation that leg used).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        with:
          # gh-2120: PINNED Dart 3.13.5 — the 3.14.0 float regressed the size
          # manifest gate self-test (artifact budgets sized on the 3.13.5
          # gh-2120: PINNED Dart 3.13.5 — the 3.14.0 float regressed the size
          # manifest gate self-test (artifact budgets sized on the 3.13.5
          # layout); bump deliberately with a budget re-baseline.
          sdk: '3.13.5'

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # gh-2181: AGENTS.md is the agent ENTRY document (harness budget
      # ~19 KB — a larger file silently disables its own tail). Ceiling
      # <= 300 lines / <= 20480 bytes; the pre-commit path runs the same
      # script via ci_fast_gate.sh stage_analyze. Wiring pinned by
      # test/agents_md_size_guard_test.dart.
      - name: AGENTS.md size ceiling guard (gh-2181)
        run: bash scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh

      # gh-2185 AC7: repo-root allow-list guard — the root carries only
      # first-class artifacts (the KEEP table); stray runtime state, logs
      # or unexpanded-${...} template-named entries fail the gate.
      # pre-commit path runs the same script via ci_fast_gate.sh
      # stage_analyze. Wiring pinned by test/root_allowlist_guard_test.dart.
      - name: Root allow-list guard (gh-2185)
        run: |
          python3 scripts/check_root_allowlist.py --self-test
          python3 scripts/check_root_allowlist.py

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)

stage_analyze() {
  # gh-2181: the AGENTS.md size ceiling runs in THIS stage — AGENTS.md
  # edits classify as docs (docs/*.md → analyze is the docs scope's only
  # stage), so a docs-only commit that regrows the entry file must fail
  # here. Same script the ci.yml static job runs (wiring pinned by
  # test/agents_md_size_guard_test.dart).
  bash scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh
  # gh-2185 AC7: repo-root allow-list — the root carries only first-class
  # artifacts; stray runtime state / logs / template-named entries fail
  # here (same script the ci.yml static job runs; wiring pinned by
  # test/root_allowlist_guard_test.dart).
  python3 scripts/check_root_allowlist.py
  echo "🔍 Running dart analyze..."
  dart analyze
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ensure_app_placeholders
    echo "🔍 Running flutter analyze (flutter_app)..."
    (cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings)
    FLUTTER_ANALYZED=1
  fi
}

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
